native.status: Built journey-v3, user-approved September 30, 2026, extended by live Walkthrough and native file/conversation navigation, message-linked checkpoints and supporting local project Run; refined Run draft/status resilience and compact conversation role/evidence with a stable transcript footer; refined checkpoint full-history search, filters, paging, exact selection and local Git meaning; refined sidebar conversation deletion with protected confirmation and retained project evidence; replaced the Switch Project menu with a native Pods overview for concurrent independent projects, removed inspector close control, and coherent compact sidebar/context entry points; refined Pods into a command station with structured live activity and guarded inline decisions; refined Pods for long-running work with honest timing, isolated filters, reader-controlled bounded feeds, guarded recovery and occlusion-aware refresh; refined Pods viewport containment with one to three columns, fixed card heights, bounded wrapping text panes, native More recovery actions and reflow-safe activity following
native.scope: native/ only; no authority over root CLI design docs or reference gallery
native.representation: Native APIs and AppKit points extend identity-only portable frontmatter. No fixed CSS colors, HTML/CSS previews, synthetic tonal ramps, or raster concept assets.

Exact 480-point acceptance is not established. Navigation follow-up frames are 1312x731 and 720x500; evidence dimensions are not layout breakpoints.

walkthrough.expandedRows: Grow with selectable detail and file links; scrolling table yields to native controls

layoutPoints.messageAndProjectTools: Trailing You and leading LUMI/activity with bounded wrapping; intrinsic checkpoint links. No new global sizing tokens. Role/completion and check/review evidence use separate lines. Jump to Latest has a reserved 28-point footer below the transcript, with zero spacing and no message overlap; hiding the button retains the footer.

checkpointPanel.qualification: Local AppKit component measurements; minimum-size extreme not visually accepted.

pods.columns: One to three equal columns from the current native content rectangle, board insets and legacy-scroller width; no window-frame breakpoint.
pods.cardHeight: Fixed for the current viewport, following available board height within 300–400 points. Bursts do not enlarge cards.
pods.activityViewport: Fills remaining card height; Pause and Latest / Resume stay in the heading row.
pods.approvalDensity: Only routine Allow Once help hides in short cards. Pending, error, unavailable and replacement messages remain visible; decisions stay outside the scrolling arguments.
pods.headerOrder: Heading/actions, native All / Working / Attention segments and search, summary/Next Request, separator, scrolling board
pods.cardOrder: Project/status; stable slot/context; instruction, timing and optional note; inline request; feed with Pause and Latest / Resume; stable Conversation / available More / Stop Agent footer
pods.compact: Current user instruction replaces the separate thread label in the context row when present; its separate instruction line hides. A monitoring note compressed into timing retains full timing in the tooltip. Next Request scrolls the waiting card into view.
pods.textViewport: Width-tracked selectable NSTextView with word wrapping, including long unbroken content; vertical growth inside clipped scroll panes with no horizontal scroller. Text insets are 8 horizontal and 6 vertical points. Exact approval payload remains unchanged.

pods.captureQualification: Final containment captures exercise three, two and one columns and an exact 640 × 480-point minimum frame. These are scoped fixture dimensions, not new global breakpoints or release/accessibility acceptance.

stateBoundaries.conversations: Negotiated durable isolated runtime context/history. Switching blocked for active/queued/uncertain/approval work; runtime refuses staged agent edits. Save current draft, invalidate pending navigation/inspection/activity, and hold composer noneditable until a fresh destination snapshot is confirmed. Adoption clears prior inspection/history controls and Walkthrough selection. Run details/output stay in the selected conversation. History never resumes execution.
stateBoundaries.drafts: Per-conversation drafts in bounded atomic workspace recovery; destination adoption restores its own text. Failed save prevents switching. Uncertain submission looked up by original ID, never replayed.
stateBoundaries.account: Private account process reuses existing OpenAI Codex OAuth/protected storage. Swift receives status/restricted browser URL/catalog availability, never credentials. Workspaces close before account change; disconnect removes local connection.
stateBoundaries.providerMigration: New dynamic-client/token-sharing contract remains separate; see JOURNEY-V3.md. No entitlement, billing or inference claim from connection/catalog status.
stateBoundaries.inspection: Read-only; browsing adds no context and filename results grant no read access. Conversation changes discard stale replies and clear inspector history. Lexical outline at most 100 declarations in displayed page; Git comparisons include earlier/external edits. Background refresh retains the preview until Reload and preserves recorded-history pages. Inspector close X/control/handler removed; compact visibility follows Conversation / Task context and context entry points.
stateBoundaries.windows: Independent workspaces; four-window product target is not an enforced source cap
stateBoundaries.walkthrough: Negotiated walkthrough-v1; follow active/approval/cancelling work over queued work, or explicitly pin loaded history. Structured events, bounded retained activity/checkpoints and ordered merges preserve partial recorded work; restart marks unfinished work interrupted without replay. Coverage and load-retry UI expose limits; not a complete audit log.
stateBoundaries.checkpoints: Negotiated checkpoints-v1; isolated local Git object store separate from repository commits, branch, HEAD and staging. Before message / After reply / Before restore · Safety copy; full date, snapshot file count, local revision, Copy Revision and workspace title. Full saved-message and revision search uses NFKC/lowercase across records before All/Flagged/Safety filtering and 100-entry paging. Matching totals, Newest, stale-offset clamp and timestamp/ID ordering. Latest navigation intent wins; pending debounced search disables old-result actions. Message links clear search/filters and resolve exact IDs across pages/existing panels. Unflagging in Flagged clears the removed target. Missing IDs leave restore disabled; explicit Refresh recovers browsing. Reviewed restore unchanged: idle preconditions, changed-file review, default Cancel, safety copy and new conversation preserving original; runtime contract retains recovery/exclusion limits.
stateBoundaries.projectRun: Negotiated project-run-v1; bounded command discovery or saved custom configuration. Opening Run or saving never executes. Literal command/folder shown; metadata revision rechecked. One process group per workspace; Stop App differs from Stop LUMI; closing stops both. Bounded console; browser-only loopback preview while running, no readiness or hosting claim. Detached descendants and user-readable files remain outside isolation guarantees. Unsaved command/folder/preview edits survive refresh, tab changes, reconnect and failed save within the window lifetime; explicit Save Command commits and Discard Edits resets to the selected target. Pending start/stop suppress duplicate requests. Unknown status disables launch/preview, preserves console and retries with Refresh recovery; failed actions reconcile actual status before another launch. Generation checks ignore obsolete replies. The actual active command/folder remains visible even if discovery omits it. No draft persistence after closing the window.
stateBoundaries.conversationDeletion: Negotiated conversation-delete-v1. Per-row inline trash is hidden without capability and disabled under conversation-switch guards, including pending work and transitions. Tooltip Delete conversation…; title-specific accessibility label. Native sheet names target, defaults to Cancel, marks Delete Conversation destructive and explains discarded draft, retained project files/checkpoints, and active versus inactive outcome. Cancel preserves draft. Confirmed active deletion opens fresh context; inactive deletion keeps current context. Interaction resumes only after fresh destination snapshot confirmation; deleted draft is removed from workspace recovery. Navigation removal retains run/checkpoint evidence; not secure erasure.
stateBoundaries.projectNavigation: Sidebar Pods first saves the current draft; failed save prevents transition. Load Projects uses a native multiple-folder chooser. Canonical paths reuse existing workspaces, each with one CLI worker. Stable opening order and loaded board are session-only. Other project work continues; no multiple concurrent workers for one canonical project. Conversation, inline decisions, guarded recovery and Stop Agent target the intended canonical path.
stateBoundaries.podActivity: Up to 30 recent structured lifecycle activities within a 24,000-character preview budget; up to 1800 characters of each event’s content and 6000 completed response characters, with explicit shortening notices and older entries dropped as needed. Exact approval payload is never shortened. No token streaming. Disclose shown versus observed counts, including after reconnection; Conversation → Walkthrough exposes retained detail/history, not a complete log. Pause, selected text, or actual user scroll/keyboard navigation away from the end freezes displayed text and preserves selection/position. Keep only displayed and newest projections; no hidden update queue. Reading paused / Paused · Updates waiting; Resume applies newest text and returns to end, Latest returns to end while live. Resize/layout alone does not pause. Following survives unchanged-text viewport/column changes, reattachment and deferred text-document reflow through a coalesced update that rechecks current pause/selection state; both scroll and document observers are removed on teardown. Conversation/run identity change resets to live. Execution, timing and approval requests continue. Live/Recorded heading follows work/review state; filtering retains each loaded pod’s reader state.
stateBoundaries.podDecisions: Complete selectable Arguments, Reason, Workspace wrap above activity without modifying the payload. Exact displayed-request Allow Once/Deny; duplicate, pending, stale, disconnected, stopping, closing and switching guards in view/workspace. A replacement freezes the displayed request and hides decisions, leaving one Review Next Request action until the replacement is explicitly loaded. Pending/errors remain visible inline, including in compact cards; only repeated routine Allow Once help hides at short height.
stateBoundaries.podMonitoring: Elapsed uses recorded start; terminal Duration freezes at recorded terminal time. Last activity age, approval Waiting … for you from worker-created request timestamp, observed activity count and explicit missing-timing copy. Day/hour formatting and start-date tooltip. Connected running work with at least two minutes of quiet shows a neutral note, never a stall diagnosis, cancellation or automatic retry. Completed, Stopped, Failed, Interrupted and Timed out remain distinct labels.
stateBoundaries.podFilters: All; Working includes running or queued work; Attention includes review, Disconnected, Check connection, Failed, Interrupted and Timed out. Case/diacritic-insensitive search over path, thread and displayed instruction. Filter only the view: preserve workers, original slot numbers/order and reader state. Hidden results retain total request count; No matching projects offers Show All Projects. Next Request clears filter and query before cycling waiting requests in stable order and scrolling the selected pod into view.
stateBoundaries.podRecovery: Native More menu contains guarded Checkpoints… and Reconnect Agent; the menu hides when neither is available. Reconnect is enabled only for an unavailable runtime whose old worker has exited, outside closing; callback rechecks availability and recovers recorded state without resubmitting tasks. Checkpoints uses existing ready-runtime/capability/window guards and reviewed history; restore retains idle-agent, queue and project-process guards. Conversation and Stop Agent remain directly available outside the text panes. Recovery targets the canonical project and is separate from feed Resume.
stateBoundaries.podRefresh: Half-second overview timer skips snapshot refresh when the window is occluded. Closing Pods invalidates its timer without stopping project workers. Scheduling is not decorative animation.

navigation.filePicker: Modeless NSPanel child of the workspace, inheriting its appearance; conversation and Stop remain available. Scope/search precede a flexible result table; status, keyboard hint, Refresh and Open Preview follow. Local picker measurements are not global tokens.
navigation.scope: Open File searches filenames and paths, not file contents. Git scope names ignore rules; plain-folder scope names hidden/generated exclusions. Conversation search says Find on this page and filters loaded titles. Code filtering remains local to the folder.
navigation.states: Clear old selectable results while searching; explicit loading, no-match, partial-scan, overlong-query and failure copy. Refresh rebuilds results; failure offers Retry and Code browsing. Open Preview disabled without valid selection. Coverage/result limits remain visible.
navigation.resultRows: Native document symbol, medium system-font filename above smaller secondary path, middle truncation, full-path tooltip and native selection.
navigation.activation: Picker arrows select; Return, double-click or Open Preview opens read-only content. Code folder selection never opens: Return/double-click/Right enters; Left returns to parent. Code file selection previews when browser and preview coexist; short layouts require Return/double-click. Opening a path reveals its parent.
navigation.focus: Escape restores previous responder; clicking the conversation dismisses without reclaiming focus. Focus Composer (Cmd-L) dismisses the picker, selects compact Conversation, makes the workspace key and makes composer first responder. Background conversation completion does not activate an inactive workspace.
navigation.availability: File menu, Actions and context header expose Open File (Cmd-P) only with a ready runtime and file-search-v1; closing, conversation transition and attached sheets prevent opening.
navigation.input: NSSearchField marked-text composition retains native handling. Debouncing and request generations schedule work and reject stale results; no decorative motion.
navigation.pods: Native command station via sidebar Pods or File → Pods (Cmd-0). Load Projects…, Project Library…, All / Working / Attention and Find project or task. Stable project order/slot identity; filtered summary retains total requests. Next Request clears filters and query, cycles waiting requests and scrolls into view. One to three viewport-sized columns with bounded wrapping payload panes; inline decisions, selectable activity with Pause / Resume, direct Conversation and Stop Agent, native More with guarded Checkpoints / Reconnect.

Noneditable during conversation transition; Cmd-L restores workspace key and composer focus. Return/IME behavior source-backed, not physically certified.

narrative.overview:
Human–agent conversation leads this macOS workspace. A quiet native shell gives the conversation room to breathe, keeps its composer available, and places project navigation and read-only evidence within reach. System typography, semantic appearance, SF Symbols, and familiar AppKit controls provide the visual character.

This records the built translation of [journey-v3](../ui-prototypes/journey-v3/), approved for implementation on September 30, 2026: projects and conversations on the left, a dominant central conversation with a unified composer, and secondary Walkthrough / Changes / Code / Run on the right. The live Walkthrough extends that system with inspectable activity and explicit follow-current or pinned-history selection. Native filename/path search and deliberate file activation connect intent to read-only evidence; conversation changes preserve separate drafts and clear stale inspection. Distinct You and LUMI messages link to reviewed local checkpoints; Run offers supporting local process control and browser preview. The same native system carries preparation, welcome, browser sign-in, the project library, and a Pods command station with run timing, project filters, contained reader-controlled activity and inline decisions across separate loaded projects. Generated concepts remain references; no raster concept ships inside the app UI.

Swift/AppKit remains the implementation. [PRODUCT.md](PRODUCT.md), [JOURNEY-V3.md](../docs/desktop/JOURNEY-V3.md), the [Walkthrough contract](../docs/desktop/WALKTHROUGH.md), and [checkpoint and Run behavior](../docs/desktop/CHECKPOINTS-AND-RUN.md) define product and runtime boundaries. This record applies only to native/. Identity-only portable frontmatter is extended by [.impeccable/design.json](.impeccable/design.json), which preserves native semantic bindings and point measurements without inventing CSS colors, web previews, or tonal ramps.
keyCharacteristics: A dominant human–agent conversation and persistent, unified native composer.
Projects and durable conversations on the left; secondary task context on the right.
A native Pods command station with stable project order, cards sized to the viewport, honest run timing, reader-controlled activity, inline approval decisions, and targeted recovery and stop actions.
Semantic light and dark appearance, system fonts, SF Symbols, and native chrome.
Readable activity and approval language with selectable technical evidence.
Explicit search scope, deliberate navigation, and a reliable return to the composer.
Message-linked project history with reviewed restore and a preserved original conversation.
Supporting local Run controls with a separate Stop App and explicit browser preview.
Runtime-owned execution, context, permissions, credentials, and task history.

rules.name: The Semantic Appearance Rule
rules.body: Preserve semantic colors and native materials in both appearances. Do not convert screenshots or system accents into fixed brand colors or synthetic tonal ramps.

rules.name: The Evidence Type Rule
rules.body: Use system prose for intent, explanation, and decisions. Reserve monospaced text for code, exact paths, arguments, and identifiers.

rules.name: The Native Depth Rule
rules.body: Let AppKit render material, focus, control state, and modality. Native screenshot shadows and bezels do not establish application shadow or blur tokens.

dos: Do keep conversation dominant and its unified composer available beside secondary context.
Do preserve native semantic colors, fonts, controls, symbols, and window behavior.
Do preserve stable Pods opening order, keep project state and decisions attributable to the exact canonical project/request, and retain the current workspace while opening another.
Do show approval arguments before decisions, preserve a reader's activity position, and distinguish structured live activity from completed responses.
Do distinguish elapsed time, terminal duration, activity age and approval wait; retain request totals and stable pod slots when filtering.
Do keep Pause / Resume local to feed reading, disclose shown versus observed history, and recover recorded state without resubmitting work.
Do size Pods from the usable viewport, contain wrapping payloads within their scroll panes, and keep approval decisions, Conversation and Stop Agent outside them.
Do follow the latest activity after viewport and text-document reflow while letting current pause and selection state take precedence.
Do keep compact workspace navigation and the selected context panel mutually exclusive.
Do fill the library's main pane, protect single-line dates, and let paths truncate.
Do use readable approval prose with exact selectable technical payloads and explicit decisions.
Do align conversation context, drafts, history, and admission with confirmed runtime state.
Do make conversation deletion explicit, default its confirmation to Cancel, discard only the deleted draft, and preserve project files and saved checkpoints.
Do distinguish read-only evidence, Git baselines, review status, and verification limits.
Do preserve explicit follow-current versus pinned history and honest stage, coverage, and issue labels.
Do state each search scope and keep folder selection separate from opening; require file activation when preview replaces the browser.
Do restore the intended native key window and responder when returning to the composer.
Do distinguish You and LUMI with alignment, role labels and symbols as well as tint.
Do resolve the exact message checkpoint, review restore scope, and preserve the original conversation and safety copy.
Do state full-history search scope, keep the latest navigation intent authoritative, distinguish snapshot counts from changed files, and name the isolated local checkpoint revision.
Do keep Save Command and Discard Edits reachable, preserve unsaved edits within the window lifetime, show the active command, and keep Stop App distinct from Stop LUMI.
Do separate role/completion from check/review evidence and reserve the 28-point Jump to Latest footer.
Do make pending actions and unknown status explicit, preserve console evidence, and reconcile status before another launch.
donts: Don't silently replace a displayed request or describe lifecycle updates as assistant token streaming.
Don't infer a stalled run from quiet activity or automatically retry it.
Don't silently substitute a checkpoint or imply complete environment recovery, server readiness, or deployment.
Don't replace Swift/AppKit with illustrative SwiftUI snippets, a web shell, or raster concepts.
Don't infer fixed palettes, tonal ramps, or a radius scale from native screenshots.
Don't promote the page outline to a language-server index or Git changes to exclusive run attribution.
Don't grant permission on default Return, replay uncertain submissions, or resume execution from history.
Don't equate connection/catalog status with subscription, billing, or inference entitlement.
Don't promote scoped reviews, synthetic fixtures, or local signing into release or accessibility certification.
Don't describe removal from conversation navigation as secure erasure of retained run or checkpoint evidence.
